images.title: One formula adds a whole row
images.purpose: Shows the formula =SUM(B3:G3) adding Nagesh's six marks into one result cell.
images.composition: A formula bar at the top, one row of six spreadsheet cells in the middle with the range outlined, and one result cell at the right end. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: At the top centre, a long white formula bar with a thin grey outline holding '=SUM(B3:G3)'. Below it, one row of six equal rectangular cells, touching, holding from left to right: 41, 43, 48, 39, 40, 39 (the number 39 appears twice: in the 4th cell and the 6th cell). The six cells share one thick teal (#0072B2) outline around the whole range. A gap, then a seventh cell at the right with a reddish purple (#CC79A7) fill holding '250' in bold. A grey arrow runs from the right end of the teal range to the result cell. No column letters, no row numbers, no other cells. Exactly 7 cells and 1 formula bar.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: SUM over a range adds every cell in it at once: here the six marks make 250.
images.description: Shows the formula =SUM(B3:G3) adding Nagesh's six marks into one result cell.

image_decisions.why: The formula is easiest to understand as a picture of the range it covers and the one cell it fills.
